activities.anchor: Double a string's vibration frequency and you hear
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the monument's tour
activities.name: skWtcEstimate

config.prompt: Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier (1722) tours every major and minor key — a prelude and fugue in each. How many keys does it visit?
config.why: 24 — every one of the 12 major and 12 minor keys, the monument to what the equal-temperament compromise bought: a keyboard that can play in any key without retuning.
config.context: Zhu Zaiyu computed the division to nine decimal places in 1584; Europe converged on the same solution over the following century.

activities.caption: true or false — the designed compromise
activities.name: skTemperJudge

statements.s: The pure fifth of a naturally buzzing string is about two cents flat of the tempered one.
statements.why: Every interval in equal temperament is microscopically impure of its simple ratio.

statements.s: Singers and string players bend towards pure ratios in sustained chords.
statements.why: The ear still wants the simple ratios the compromise flattened.

statements.s: Maqām, rāga and gamelan divide the octave differently on purpose.
statements.why: Non-Western systems divide the octave differently on purpose — the twelve-note grid is one dialect, not the law.

statements.s: Equal temperament is the natural tuning.
statements.why: It is a designed compromise — temperament is engineering, not nature; it optimises for modulation and pays in purity.

activities.anchor: Real minor-key music actually uses three versions
activities.caption: file each trait under its minor version
activities.name: skMinorBuckets

config.prompt: One sad colour, three versions — file each trait:

items.label: for descending lines and modal colour
raised 7th, creating the leading tone that pulls home

config.why: Composers wanted the sad colour and the gravitational pull of a leading note — so all three versions share the field.

activities.caption: pair each modulation with the weather it brings
activities.name: skModulateMatch

config.prompt: Changing key mid-piece — pair each move with what the listener feels:

pairs.left: modulate to the dominant (up a fifth)
a pop chorus moved up a semitone

config.why: Most modulation moves between closely related keys via a pivot chord that belongs to both worlds — the listener hears not a rupture but a change of weather.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — why the pentatonic cannot miss
activities.name: skPentaCloze

config.text: The pentatonic is the major scale minus its two most awkward steps; with no %%0%% neighbours, any ordering of its notes sounds %%1%% — five carefully chosen notes out of twelve that cannot %%2%%.
config.hint: One gap size, one sound quality, one thing the notes can never do to each other.

activities.anchor: Two great systems organise pitch without Western chords
activities.caption: walk the decision — the sound the grid cannot spell
activities.name: skRagaBranch

config.root: You want colour the twelve-note grid cannot spell. Walk the options:

choices.label: Maqām Rast's 'E half-flat', tuned by ear on the oud
choices.feedback: A real pitch with a real emotional address — a microtone between the Western semitones.

choices.label: A rāga's rules of movement over the tanpura drone
choices.feedback: Ascent, descent, signature phrases and an assigned time of day carry the meaning.

choices.label: Spell it on the piano
choices.feedback: The Western page can only approximate it.

maqam.text: Maqām names melodic territories built from small cells (ajnās) using microtones, fixed by levers on the qanun — no Western key signature can spell Rast.

raga.text: A rāga is a melodic being-with-rules — required ascent and descent, ornaments, an emotional character (rasa), often an assigned time of day — depth without chord change.

piano.text: A Western page can only approximate what maqām Rast or rāga Bhairavi actually ask for — the sound the notation struggles with is often the most local and most expressive part.

config.why: Both systems treat pitch as a landscape with customs — a shared lesson of the drone traditions is that the 'home note' idea is deeper than the chords built on top of it.

activities.caption: put the tempered third on the cents scale
activities.name: skThirdPlace

config.prompt: The pure major third (5:4) is 386 cents. Equal temperament widens it — place the tempered major third (in cents):
config.why: 400 against a pure 386 — 14 cents flat of perfection, which is why choirs and string quartets that tune by ear drift sharper than pianos on sustained major chords.
